title: Neutron stars can have a maximum mass of about 2.2 solar masses.
purpose: Discuss the upper mass limit (Tolman-Oppenheimer-Volkoff limit).
narration: What determines the maximum mass of a neutron star? Astronomers call this the Tolman-Oppenheimer-Volkoff limit, and it's roughly 2.2 times the mass of our Sun. This boundary separates stable neutron stars from collapse into a black hole. Let's explore why this limit is so important.
